run.question:
Customers reported slow checkout for the last hour. Check our Datadog APM
traces for the checkout-service and find which downstream call is slow.

report.summary: Datadog APM is not a configured data source for this Run (available sources are elasticsearch, jaeger, kubernetes, prometheus), so Datadog traces for the checkout service could not be read at all. The tracing backend that is configured (Jaeger, target m0-otel-20260909) and the Prometheus target both answered every attempt with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (traces_list_services, traces_search, traces_list_operations, get_metric_names, get_all_labels, get_prometheus_target, execute_prometheus_instant_query), and Elasticsearch held only two internal system indices, no application logs or trace documents. Without trace or latency-metric data I could not identify which downstream call of checkout is slow, and no root cause is named. What the reachable Kubernetes evidence does show: in namespace otel-demo all 22 pods are Running and Ready, including checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n (2 restarts); checkout's own logs from 08:21:27Z to 09:00:46Z show only successful order flows with no error lines, and in the sampled lines the whole PlaceOrder -> payment charge -> confirmation-email path completed within roughly 13-42 ms, so these samples do not exhibit a slow checkout; checkout's configured downstreams are cart:8080, currency:8080, email:8080, payment:8080, product-catalog:8080 and shipping:8080 (shipping itself calls quote:8080), plus flagd:8013 for feature flags, and every flag in the flagd-config ConfigMap (including paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, cartFailure, adHighCpu, imageSlowLoad) has defaultVariant off in the config as read at 09:01Z, so no fault/latency injection was switched on there. A cluster-wide pod restart wave hit all otel-demo pods at 08:04:18-08:05:10Z, before the sampled checkout traffic, and the Prometheus read-only proxy pod has 6 restarts with last termination Error/exit 1 and an nginx '[emerg] host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090"' log line. The slow downstream call remains undetermined.

claims.text: In namespace otel-demo all 22 application pods are Running with container ready=true, including checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n, payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d, shipping-6fc5f694db-9sq2c, quote-75774ddb4c-kpbqh, currency-6db8974b78-8g7s7, product-catalog-777f5468d4-hc8rj and email-6cd97b67f9-nhnxc; restart counts are 2 for these application pods (4 for kube-state-metrics, 6 for prometheus-readonly-proxy).

checkout pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n logged 278 lines between 2026-11-22T08:21:27Z and 09:00:46Z, all of severity info and only of the forms '[PlaceOrder] user_id=... user_currency=...', 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' and 'order confirmation email sent to ...'; no error, exception or failure line appears in that sample.

Within those sampled checkout log sequences the '[PlaceOrder]' line to 'payment went through' interval was about 13.2 ms (08:21:44.462Z -> 08:21:44.475Z), 13.5 ms (08:22:47.439Z -> 08:22:47.453Z), 19.2 ms (08:38:34.387Z -> 08:38:34.406Z), 30.0 ms (08:54:37.326Z -> 08:54:37.356Z) and 14.6 ms (08:59:50.955Z -> 08:59:50.970Z), and 'payment went through' to 'order confirmation email sent' added about 9.6-12.3 ms.

The checkout Deployment configures its downstream dependencies as CART_ADDR=cart:8080, CURRENCY_ADDR=currency:8080, EMAIL_ADDR=http://email:8080, PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080, PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR=product-catalog:8080, SHIPPING_ADDR=shipping:8080, FLAGD_HOST=flagd/FLAGD_PORT=8013, with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout and memory limit 20Mi; the shipping Deployment sets QUOTE_ADDR=http://quote:8080.

The flagd-config ConfigMap ('demo.flagd.json', namespace otel-demo) defines fault/latency flags productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, and every one of them has defaultVariant 'off' in the content read at 2026-11-22T09:01Z.

Events in namespace otel-demo show every application pod (including ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, frontend, frontend-proxy, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart, flagd, jaeger, otel-collector, prometheus) receiving SandboxChanged at 08:04:18Z followed by Pulled/Created/Started between 08:04:18Z and 08:05:10Z, i.e. a cluster-wide restart wave finished before the first sampled checkout log line at 08:21:27Z.

Pod prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn (nginx:1.28.0-alpine) has 6 container restarts with last termination reason Error and exit code 1, and its previous container instance logged '2026/11/22 08:04:37 [emerg] 1#1: host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090" in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf:22' plus 'nginx: [emerg] host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090"'.

The Elasticsearch backend matched by pattern '*' with expand_wildcards=all contains only two indices, .ds-.logs-deprecation.elasticsearch-default-2026.11.22-000001 (1 doc) and .ds-ilm-history-7-2026.11.22-000001 (3 docs); no application log or trace index is present.
Services jaeger-query (16686) and prometheus (9090) exist in namespace otel-demo as ClusterIP services, so the observability backends the tools target are deployed in this cluster.

The sampled checkout log pairs do not show a slow checkout: the entire pre-charge path (which per checkout's configuration includes cart:8080, product-catalog:8080, currency:8080, shipping:8080/quote:8080 and payment:8080) plus the post-charge shipping-email step completed within roughly 23-42 ms in every sampled PlaceOrder sequence between 08:21Z and 09:00Z, so this log sample gives no support to a large latency in one of those calls during that period.

The payment pod's logs read over the window contain exactly one line matching the error pattern, an 08:04:24Z Node gRPC 'MetadataLookupWarning: ... incorrect Metadata-Flavor header' line; no charge-request failure or paymentUnreachable-style error appears in the 197 lines read through 09:01:23Z.

If checkout really was slow during the reported last hour, the slow span lies in one of its configured downstream calls (cart:8080, currency:8080, product-catalog:8080, shipping:8080 which calls quote:8080, payment:8080, email:8080) or in checkout itself, but which one cannot be selected because no per-span or per-rpc latency series could be read in this Run.

The repeated failure of the pod prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn (6 restarts, last termination Error/exit 1, nginx failing to resolve upstream 'prometheus:9090') may be why every Prometheus tool call returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, but the tool error carries no upstream detail, so the link between that pod and the tool outage is unverified.

Obtain per-dependency latency for checkout from a working tracing or metrics path before naming the slow call: either enable the Datadog APM integration, or query Jaeger at jaeger-query:16686 for checkout spans and Prometheus for rpc_client_duration_milliseconds / traces_span_metrics_calls_total once prometheus:9090 is reachable again.

gaps: Datadog APM is not among the configured data sources for this Run (only elasticsearch, jaeger, kubernetes and prometheus are available), so no Datadog trace, span or APM metric for the checkout service could be inspected; the question's requested source is unavailable rather than empty.

All Jaeger calls (traces_list_services, traces_search for service 'checkout' over 08:50-09:00Z and 08:00-09:00Z, traces_list_operations) returned status error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE against target m0-otel-20260909, so no span, parent reference or span duration was returned and the slow downstream call cannot be attributed.

All Prometheus calls (get_metric_names, get_all_labels, get_prometheus_target for job 'otel-collector', execute_prometheus_instant_query on traces_span_metrics_calls_total) returned status error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so rpc_client_duration_milliseconds, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket and traces_span_metrics_calls_total hold no readable values; latency of individual downstream calls is unknown, not zero.

No latency baseline exists for the reported 'last hour': with no trace or metric samples I cannot establish when checkout latency began to deviate, so the reports of slow checkout are unverified by telemetry.

Application logs carry no per-dependency timing, so the 13-42 ms PlaceOrder sequences only bound the total of the sampled requests and cannot show which dependency (cart, currency, product-catalog, shipping/quote, payment, email) took how long.

The flagd-config content was read at 2026-11-22T09:01Z (after the incident window's end); I could not verify which variant was in effect during 08:00-09:00Z, and no change history or audit of flagd flag state is available.

shipping-6fc5f694db-9sq2c and quote-75774ddb4c-kpbqh log queries with an error filter returned no matching lines (status no_data), which only shows that query matched nothing and cannot be used as proof those services were error-free.

The cause of the cluster-wide pod restart wave at 08:04:18-08:05:10Z is not visible in the evidence (no owning controller SuccessfulDelete/SuccessfulCreate events, no node events except normal allocatable/disk/memory messages), and its relation to the checkout slowness report is unknown.
No Datadog, Elasticsearch APM or node/pod resource metric data was available to check CPU throttling (checkout's memory limit is 20Mi) as an alternative cause of slow checkout.
next_steps: Connect the Datadog APM integration, or hand over a Jaeger/Prometheus endpoint that answers, then query checkout server spans and client spans per downstream operation (cart, currency, product-catalog, shipping/quote, payment, email) to rank the slowest child span during 08:00-09:00Z.

Once Prometheus at prometheus:9090 is reachable, evaluate rate/increase over rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count and histogram quantiles of rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_bucket grouped by service_name/rpc_service/rpc_method for the checkout service, and traces_span_metrics_calls_total by span_name and status_code.

Check whether prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn's 'host not found in upstream "prometheus:9090"' startup failure recurs and whether it is on the query path used for metrics, since it has 6 restarts and a last termination of Error/exit 1.
Confirm the flagd flag variants that were in effect during 08:00-09:00Z from flagd telemetry or a flag change audit, since the ConfigMap read at 09:01Z shows all flags with defaultVariant off.
Review checkout container memory limit 20Mi and any CPU limits with node/cAdvisor data to rule out resource-induced latency in checkout itself.
